title: Under Direct Edit the Responsible Party proposes the change but a Facilitator makes it
content:
A.1.13.1.3.1 sets out the Direct Edit process. The Responsible Party "must post on the Sky Forum their proposed changes to the Active Data," after which a Facilitator acts: for data in the Sky Core Atlas "the Core Facilitator must confirm that the Responsible Party has the authority to request a Direct Edit, and then modify the Atlas to reflect the Responsible Party's proposed change," while for data in an Agent Artifact the Agent's Operational Facilitator does the same.

Despite the name, "Direct Edit" gives the Responsible Party no write access. The obligation to maintain the data and the ability to alter the canonical document are held by different parties, with an authority check in between and a public Forum record of what was requested. That makes every change attributable to a request and comparable against it — the Facilitator's edit can be audited against the post that asked for it.

The section also constrains customization: a Controller may "specify unique requirements in addition to the general 'Direct Edit' Update Process," but they must be stated in the Controller Document (possibly by citation) and "may supplement, but cannot conflict with, any aspect of the 'Direct Edit' Update Process defined herein."

That one-way layering matters. Controllers can only make the process stricter, never looser, so no amount of per-document configuration can erode the baseline — and a reader of any Controller knows the general process still applies in full.
description: The party obligated to maintain Active Data posts the change on the Forum; the Core or Operational Facilitator confirms their authority and then edits the Atlas themselves.
